name: Boho

influenced_by: 19th-century Parisian bohemian artist and writer communities

eras: 2000s (as a named trend), rooted in 1960s-70s bohemian style

media.title: Sienna Miller and Kate Moss's 2004–2005 Glastonbury festival styling
media.note: widely cited in fashion-media retrospectives as a key moment for the 2000s boho wave

reacts_against: mid-2000s fashion's polished, body-conscious glamour, offering a softer, more undone alternative drawn from an older bohemian and hippie tradition.
article: "Bohemian" as a term for artists and writers living outside conventional social norms dates to 19th-century Paris, where it was (inaccurately) associated with Romani immigrants the French assumed had come via Bohemia, in today's Czech Republic. Fashion borrowed the word repeatedly over the following century, but "boho" as a specific, heavily marketed 2000s trend crystallized around 2004–2005, when fashion media fixed on the festival styling of celebrities like Sienna Miller and Kate Moss at Glastonbury — flowing fabric, suede fringe, layered jewelry, a softened, shoppable descendant of 1960s-70s hippie dress with most of that era's political content left out. The 2000s wave was substantial enough to support its own retail category for most of a decade before fading, and boho has resurfaced periodically since as a recurring seasonal trend reference rather than a single continuous movement, each revival pulling slightly different pieces from the same long bohemian-hippie lineage.
